q: Can I use HSN codes on GST invoices to classify purchases for Scope 3?
title: Using HSN codes to classify Scope 3
short: Yes, as a classification aid. The HSN code tells you what was bought, such as flat-rolled steel, plastics or machinery, which points to the Scope 3 category and the material. It does not give you an emission factor. You still need the quantity and unit from the invoice and a factor chosen for that material.
audience: Accountants and sustainability leads in India

sections.h: What an HSN code tells you
ul: The chapter (first two digits) gives the broad material: 39 plastics, 48 paper and paperboard, 72 iron and steel, 73 articles of iron or steel, 76 aluminium, 84 machinery.
The heading (four digits) narrows it: 7208 is hot-rolled flat steel, 8457 is machining centres.
SAC codes in chapter 99 cover services, such as 9965 for goods transport.
p: GST invoices for business buyers must show at least four digits, or six digits for suppliers with turnover above ₹5 crore, so most B2B lines carry a usable code.

ul: Materials and parts you consume, such as steel coil or plastic granules: Category 1, purchased goods.
Machinery and equipment you capitalise (chapters 84 and 85 mostly): Category 2, capital goods. Confirm with your fixed asset register, because the same code can be a spare part you expense.
Fuel (chapter 27) burned on site: Scope 1, not Scope 3. Electricity (2716): Scope 2.
Freight services: Category 4 or 9, depending on who pays.

p: There is no official mapping from HSN codes to emission factors. A code covers a product class, while emissions depend on how and where the item was made: steel from a blast furnace and steel from a scrap-based electric furnace share a code but differ widely. Pick the factor separately, from the supplier if possible, and record its source.

ul: Wrong or generic codes on small suppliers' invoices: read the description too.
Units: steel by the tonne, cable by the metre, fasteners by the piece. The factor's unit must match.
Mixed invoices: one invoice with several codes needs each line classified separately.

example.title: Worked example: one invoice line
lines: Line: HSN 7208, hot-rolled steel coil, 10 tonnes
Category: 1, purchased goods; material: flat steel
Factor (proxy, no supplier figure): about 1.9 t CO2 per t steel, worldsteel global average
10 x 1.9 = 19 t CO2, labelled as an average-data estimate
example.note: The HSN code chose the category and material; the factor came from a separate, named source.

senseible: Senseible classifies invoice lines by HSN or SAC code first, and by keyword only when the unit agrees. A line gets a figure only when its quantity and unit match an approved factor for that category and material; otherwise it shows Needs Data.
